issue.title: delete_line_range strips the trailing newline when end_line exceeds EOF; insert_at_line's documented append does not exist
issue.body:
### What happened?

Part of the editor-tool AX evaluation that produced #3033. Fixtures in `tmp/editortest/`; every case below was executed.

The range editors (`read_line_range`, `insert_at_line`, `delete_line_range`) are mostly well behaved — deletion and insertion echo the affected content back, which is genuinely good for verification. But `delete_line_range` silently strips a file's trailing newline in one specific case, and `insert_at_line`'s documented append behaviour does not exist.

### What did you expect to happen?

That deleting the last line of a file produces the same file regardless of how I spell the range, and that the documented append-past-EOF behaviour works.

---

## 1. `delete_line_range` strips the trailing newline when `end_line` exceeds EOF

Minimal repro. Two files, both `aaa\nbbb\nccc\n`, both asked to delete the last line:

    delete_line_range(start_line: 3, end_line: 3)   => aaa\nbbb\n     (correct)
    delete_line_range(start_line: 3, end_line: 999) => aaa\nbbb       (trailing newline lost)

Verified by hexdump: `6161 610a 6262 620a` vs `6161 610a 6262 62`.

Same intent, same file, different result depending on whether the caller clamps the range — and clamping is the natural thing to write when you mean "delete from here to the end". The result is a file with no POSIX final newline, which trips `eol-last`, Prettier, and shows up as a spurious diff hunk.

Root cause, `packages/tools/src/tools/delete_line_range.ts:173-195`:

    const lines = content.split('\n');          // "aaa\nbbb\nccc\n" -> ['aaa','bbb','ccc','']
    const count = this.params.end_line - this.params.start_line + 1;   // never clamped
    lines.splice(startIndex, count);
    const newContent = lines.join('\n');

`split('\n')` on a newline-terminated file yields a phantom trailing `''` that *is* the final newline. With `end_line: 3` the splice removes only `'ccc'` and the `''` survives. With `end_line: 999`, `count` is 997, so the splice consumes the `''` too and the newline is gone.

Fix: clamp `count` to the real line count, or preserve the trailing newline explicitly when the original content ended with one.

## 2. The same phantom line leaks into user-facing line counts

Because `totalLines = lines.length` counts the phantom `''`, bounds errors report a length one greater than the file has:

    insert_at_line(line_number: 999) on a 7-line file
      -> "line_number 999 exceeds file length (8)"

    delete_line_range(start_line: 100) on an 8-line file
      -> "start_line 100 exceeds file length (9)"

The caller then has to guess whether "8" means there are 8 lines (there are 7) — and the off-by-one matters, because the valid append position *is* the phantom index. It works, but only by accident of two bugs agreeing.

## 3. `insert_at_line`'s documented append behaviour does not exist

The tool description states:

> If 'line_number' is greater than the total lines, the content will be appended to the end of the file.

It is not appended; it is rejected:

    insert_at_line(line_number: 999) -> {"error":"line_number 999 exceeds file length (8)"}

Source (`insert_at_line.ts:179`) guards `line_number > totalLines + 1` and returns an error. Either implement the documented append, or fix the description. (See the related cross-cutting issue: the *helpful* half of this error message never reaches the caller.)

## 4. `read_line_range` warns "content has been truncated" on its own normal use

Every range read, including one that returns exactly what was asked for, is prefixed with:

    IMPORTANT: The file content has been truncated.
    Status: Showing lines 1-5 of 14 total lines.
    Action: To read more of the file, you can use the 'read_line_range' tool with adjusted 'start_line' and 'end_line' parameters.

Asking a range-reading tool for a range and being told the result is "truncated" — in capitals, marked IMPORTANT — is noise on the tool's intended path, and the suggested "action" is the call I just made. Reserve the warning for genuine truncation (a range clipped by an output-size limit) and otherwise report the range plainly.

## 5. Out-of-bounds reads return an incoherent range and no error

    read_line_range(start_line: 20, end_line: 30) on a 14-line file
      -> "Status: Showing lines 15-14 of 14 total lines." with empty content, no error

"Showing lines 15-14" is an inverted, impossible range, and the empty body reads like "this part of the file is empty" rather than "you asked past the end". It should say `start_line 20 is beyond end of file (14 lines)`.

---

## What works well

- `delete_line_range` echoes the deleted text back in the response, and `insert_at_line` echoes what it inserted. That is exactly right for a line-oriented editor: it makes the change verifiable without a follow-up read, which is precisely what the other editing tools fail to provide.
- Inclusive `end_line` semantics are correct, including blank lines at the boundary.
- `insert_at_line` handles content with *and* without a trailing newline correctly, and preserves the file's final newline in both cases. Its newline handling is strictly better than `delete_line_range`'s.
- `insert_at_line` correctly refuses to insert anywhere but line 1 in a non-existent file.

## Suggested fixes, in priority order

1. Clamp the delete count so `end_line` past EOF cannot consume the trailing newline. (item 1)
2. Make `insert_at_line` match its description, or correct the description. (item 3)
3. Report real line counts, not the phantom split artefact. (item 2)
4. Stop labelling ordinary range reads as truncated. (item 4)
5. Return a real error for reads that start past EOF. (item 5)

### Client information

0.11.0-nightly, branch at 75a5cb5d95

### Anything else we need to know?

Related: #3033 (apply_patch AX) and the `ast_edit` AX issue filed alongside this.

steps:
Create two files a.txt and b.txt, each containing exactly `aaa
bbb
ccc
` (three lines, each ending with a newline), for example with printf.
Call delete_line_range on a.txt with start_line 3 and end_line 3, and on b.txt with start_line 3 and end_line 999, then compare both files byte by byte with xxd.
expected: Both files end up as `aaa\nbbb\n`, keeping the trailing newline regardless of how the end of the range is spelled.
defect:
With end_line 999 the trailing newline is also removed (`aaa
bbb` vs `aaa
bbb
`; hexdump `6161 610a 6262 62`).

fault location.explanation: split('\n') leaves a phantom '' element for the final newline, totalLines counts it, and count = end_line - start_line + 1 is never clamped, so an over-long range splices the phantom element away; PR #3053 models lines without the phantom element (lineEditing helpers) and clamps the range.

The same phantom element inflates totalLines in the 'exceeds file length' error, and appending past EOF is rejected although the description promises it; PR #3053 fixes the line model and the documented append behaviour.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/vybestack/llxprt-code/pull/3053. In v0.10.0, delete_line_range splits the file with content.split('\n'); for a newline-terminated file this yields a trailing empty string that represents the final newline. totalLines includes it, and the splice count is end_line - start_line + 1 without clamping to the real number of lines. With end_line equal to the last line the phantom element survives and join('\n') restores the final newline, but with end_line beyond EOF the splice also removes the phantom element and the file loses its trailing newline. insert_at_line uses the same line model, so its errors report one line too many, and it rejects line numbers past EOF although its description says the content will be appended. Commit 5c2dc30 (PR #3053, 'Fix range-editor tools' phantom trailing-newline line model') adds shared line-editing helpers that keep the trailing newline separate, clamps ranges, and aligns insert_at_line with its documented append. The fix first ships in v0.11.0, the pinned version, so the case is tested at v0.10.0.
